attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, said in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'No path to doing so in the future' is a firm, unhedged forecast. The proposition also states the present no-profit premise, which the contract fairly leaves unscored. It drops the 'make more money than they cost' framing, but the meaning is close.

contract.note: The claim sets no horizon, but the contract takes the six-year window from the speaker's own sentence. That gives him a finite, generous test. Reading 'profit' as cumulative recovery of deployment costs is ordinary in this capex context. Gross margin, operating profit and payback could each give a different result.

evidence.note: Oracle disclosure dated before the cutoff, stating a 32% gross margin on AI capacity delivered in FQ3 2026. It is the company's statement about itself, not an independent finding, and it covers gross margin, not cumulative cost recovery. It also doesn't isolate the GPU cohort, so it can't trigger early resolution.

reviews.rationale: The forecast's six-year window ends 2031-12-08, after the evaluation date. Oracle's positive gross margin weighs against a gross-margin reading. But it is a company disclosure that doesn't show any deployment recovering its full capital and operating costs, so the early-resolution rule isn't met. No deployment-level accounts were found that settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron states the figure in his own voice, based on his own reporting.

semantics.note: Keeps his 'in the same period' wording without settling which period it means, and keeps the $8.67B figure. It is correctly classed as a historical observation.

contract.note: Taking 'same period' as CY Q3 2025, from the sentence just before, is the grammatical reading. The contract also keeps the January–September alternative, so it doesn't stretch the claim either way. Which period applies, and Azure-only versus all-provider spending, would change the result.

evidence.note: Register article from Nov 2025, before the cutoff. It describes about $8.7B as Azure-only spending for Jan–Sep 2025 and credits the figure to Zitron's own documents. It isn't independent and covers a different period and provider scope than the Q3 reading.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence repeats Zitron's own leaked figure, which the contract rules out as independent confirmation. It also describes the spending as Azure-only over nine months, not one quarter. Under the contract, a January–September total doesn't settle the Q3 claim. No independent Q3 record was found.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion and his own calculation, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Adding 'AI' to 'profit' is supported by the surrounding AI-capex context. It leaves out the roughly $605B capex basis, but keeps the $1.21T hole as his estimate. It is correctly classed as an observation.

contract.note: Reading the claim as AI-attributable profit is ordinary in context. The contract correctly says company-wide or segment profits don't count. How AI is scoped (generative only, or including recommendations) and how profit is defined would change the result.

evidence.note: Meta's CEO said before the post that AI returns are showing in the core business. It is a qualitative company statement with no measured AI profit, so it is relevant but not decisive.
Amazon reported positive AWS operating income for Q3 2025. AWS covers far more than AI, so this doesn't show AI-specific profit.
Alphabet doesn't assign its shared AI R&D costs to any segment, so its segment results can't give a full picture of AI-specific profit.

reviews.rationale: No company in the packet reports AI-specific revenue matched to its costs. Meta's statement about returns is qualitative and self-reported. AWS and Google segment profits mix AI with other business. Nobody has reconstructed the $605B capex figure or the $1.21T gap. The evidence neither confirms nor refutes the 'not a dollar of profit' claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' forecast with 'at some point' as its horizon. The proposition keeps all three steps of his chain and the 'unprofitable, unsustainable' description.

contract.note: Requiring all three steps for support matches his chain. The contract correctly says the claim can't be contradicted just because time passes, since there is no deadline. Reading 'forced to stop' as a broad, sustained pullback is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Crunchbase data for Q3 2026, published before the cutoff: AI startups raised $102B, down from the prior two quarters but still large. So the first step hadn't happened. With no deadline, that isn't a contradiction.

CNBC, 2026-10-15: CoreWeave's credit default swaps reached distress levels, a sign of debt stress among GPU buyers. It touches the third step but isn't tied to a VC pullback or to startups failing to pay.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. By the evaluation date, AI venture funding was still very large and no startup was documented failing to pay compute providers, so the early-resolution rule isn't met. Debt stress at CoreWeave touches only the last step of the chain. Because there is no deadline, the lack of the event so far is not a failure.
